method: the comparison page loads each PNG into a canvas and re-derives the region boundaries from raw pixels only (canvas getImageData), before any annotation overlay is drawn. Independent of the DOM getBoundingClientRect values in measurements.json.

definitions.firstPanelColumnX: first x whose column is panel-white (#ffffff, tol 3) for the next 24 consecutive columns (y 100..860) - the rail | surface boundary
definitions.firstPanelRowY: first y whose row is panel-white (>=90% of x 8..1432, tol 3) - the top of the app surfaces
definitions.railBgFraction: fraction of a below-the-buttons rail band (x 10..46, y 300..780) that is window background (#f7f7f8, tol 6). The band deliberately avoids the rail controls so a toggle's active/hover CSS fill cannot colour the metric.

reading.vertical: reference first panel-white row = 48/49; current = 9. The 40px difference is the drawn title bar the reference renders and #42 removes. It matches the DOM delta of exactly 40px in measurements.json.
reading.horizontal: the rail | surface boundary is column 56/57 in both, i.e. the 56px rail (--rail-width) plus the 1px pane border/antialias. Horizontal geometry is unchanged.
reading.railFill: the app's rail is 100% window background in the sampled band (no drawn chrome strip); the reference rail is 93.9-95.0% background because the wireframe draws decorative rail icons there. A drawn-content difference, not a geometry difference.
reading.reference 02 firstPanelColumnX null: expected: the reference screen 02 sidebar is text-dense, so no run of 24 consecutive columns stays >=90% panel-white; the current sidebar is sparser. The row probe (content-insensitive) is the reliable one and it agrees at 48 vs 9.
